item.description:
Author: segarule
Posted: Fri Oct 30, 2026 9:59 am (GMT 0)

Aranya wrote
segarule wrote
Quote
Yes, a subforum for the AI threads sounds like a good idea.
Maybe it´s time we create our forum. Forum created by AI. AI moderators; AI competition; AI voters and AI judges! LOL. Seriously, maybe we will need go out in future.


What objection do you have to having a subforum for AI-generated projects while keeping the rest of the forum for non AI projects?

Me? None. But I'm noticing a certain look of prejudice and hostility. Virtually every platform is seeing games being ported with AI: Amiga, Mega Drive, NES, Game Boy, etc. And the messages we're seeing are from people who are bothered by the number of games being released? That doesn't make sense.

Are developers feeling discouraged? But wasn't this all supposed to be about having fun? If it's about having fun, then it shouldn't matter what others are doing.

However, the trend seems to be that this space will eventually be left to purists only. That's why the suggestion is to leave now rather than wait to be pushed out.

In my opinion, there's room for all these different approaches to coexist.

Now, lets see this rule:
We may want to clarify this a little better before the competition happens, but in the current climate the general intention is that an entry where e.g. ~10% of the work is aided by AI would likely be accepted (e.g. an additional language, selected artwork), but an entry where ~50% of the work is done by AI wouldn't. This is not a firm rule here, but sort of aim to provide a general background intent about this (Bock)

Im curious to know who will use and who dont will use and mainly who will use in secret. I created this thread for all AI port creators put the roms and gamers have fun but is flooding. What about a topic "AI criticism" only for users continue hatred?
PS: This dont have value but in 1 port i wasted hours messaging, editing, searching, testing in hardware, fixing. But this dont count, so i dont will entry in any competition.

item.description:
Author: undeveloper
Posted: Fri Oct 30, 2026 8:40 am (GMT 0)

And for the record: I think a separate sub-forum would be the most appropriate and equitable way to organise this. I don't think that AI work should be excluded from the community or marginalised, because there are sufficient people who engage with it enthusiastically. I also think putting it into one big mega-thread would be treating it like a second-class citizen and asking those participating in it to work with different ergonomics to everyone else which isn't fair.

We already use sub-forums to organise broad topics based on interest area, and we should continue to use that precedent.

item.title: Main :: RE: Ports created by [AI]
item.description:
Author: undeveloper
Posted: Fri Oct 30, 2026 8:29 am (GMT 0)

Aranya wrote
In my opinion, although I'm neither an AI user nor someone who has ever done any programming, I can only see objections coming from a section of the community which, in my view, doesn't seem to have taken very well to the "democratisation" of access to creating content for the console.

I'm sorry, I normally don't like to engage in online arguments like this, but some of your recent comments have been so full of nonsense.

What on earth are you actually talking about?

Democratisation? Do you realise how loaded your language is? You advised someone on another thread to "think about it" recently. I would strongly suggest you take your own advice and think very hard about what you are really saying before you start wading into a discussion throwing loaded accusations around that those who reasonably raise concerns about the nature of content in a community they are invested in is implicitly acting in bad faith or "undemocratically".

Many of the people who are involved in this forum have a professional connection to the software industry. Many do not. Many are using AI professionally now. Many are not. Many members have been actively helping to make it easier for people to get involved in retro game dev in many different ways. Many have not. There are many more dimensions to consider but one thing is true - there is no general correlation between the many diverse and wonderful people who use this forum and their stance on AI.

It is true that emotions are running high around this. This is to be expected - it's a big change and change is hard. Most of the long time members of this forum are lovely people who care deeply about the subject and feel like they have a stake in it. Most of them are - if you actually pay attention - engaging in a process of reasonable and civil, if sometimes heated, debate while they wrestle with their own feelings and opinions at the same time.

By the way, THAT is democracy.

You are not helping by slinging thinly veiled accusations around about people's inner motivations. My advice before the next time you say something like this: Think about it.

item.title: Main :: RE: Ports created by [AI]
item.description:
Author: Aranya
Posted: Fri Oct 30, 2026 8:07 am (GMT 0)

In my opinion, although I'm neither an AI user nor someone who has ever done any programming, I can only see objections coming from a section of the community which, in my view, doesn't seem to have taken very well to the "democratisation" of access to creating content for the console.

I understand the desire to make a distinction and clearly identify which projects are AI-assisted and which aren't, since the effort involved and the merit are completely different. That's only fair. However, being opposed to everything made with AI seems absurd to me, as long as it doesn't affect people's jobs, steal other people's work, or cause anyone any harm.

I have nothing against an AI-enhanced Mortal Kombat, but I would be absolutely against an AI-generated Razing Core 2 made without Badcomputer's permission.

Furthermore, I believe that providing feedback on AI-assisted creations can encourage their creators to refine and develop their work further, rather than immediately jumping into a new project just to get likes or attract attention.
